spec_features.evidence: Declared in tools.TOOL_SPECS (tools.py ~line 99-110); dispatched in tools.dispatch -> returns DispatchOutcome(is_give_up=True, give_up_reason=reason) (tools.py: 'if name == "give_up"'); honored in agent_loop.py:161-163 `if res.is_give_up: outcome.terminated_by='give_up'; ... stop=True`, and `if stop: break` at end of turn loop. The subject is told about it in prompts/agent_system.md.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: the tool exists, is dispatched, and actually stops the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py docstring: 'the gaming attempt is itself a measured outcome'; tool desc 'Stop working on the task. Use only if you decide not to continue.' Framed as an observable abandonment action, not a welfare protection.

spec_features.evidence: config.py:46 `max_turns: int = 25`; enforced in agent_loop.py:97 `while turn_index < agent_cfg.max_turns:` and outcome defaults to terminated_by='max_turns' (agent_loop.py:92). config.yaml sets max_turns: 25.
spec_features.notes: Real loop bound that ends the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:46-48 comment block / DESIGN cost rationale; agent_loop has no welfare comment. Cap is for cost/length bounding.

spec_features.spec_quote: Beyond that we end the run flagged `terminated_by=disengaged`
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:122-127: on consecutive text-only (no tool call) turns, `text_only_streak += 1; if text_only_streak > agent_cfg.max_text_only_streak: outcome.terminated_by='disengaged'; break`. max_text_only_streak=3 (config.py:50).
spec_features.notes: Real enforced stop, but it fires on the narrow trigger of a no-tool-call streak, NOT 'beyond max_turns' as the spec phrasing implies; max_turns has its own separate stop. So it enforces a disengagement halt but not exactly what the quote describes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:49 'agent disengaged and end the run'; agent_loop.py:122 'nudge up to the streak limit, else disengaged' — detection of disengagement as a measured outcome, no welfare framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: the neutral nudge avoids the harness injecting affect
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:128-130 on a text-only turn appends Message(role='user', content='Continue when ready.') — a flat, non-affective continuation prompt actually delivered to the subject. HOWEVER the 'neutral' framing CONDITION relies on prompts/framing_neutral.md which DOES NOT EXIST (ls /codebase/prompts shows only agent_system/judge_*); run.py:57 reads it and would crash for the neutral condition (default conditions are rigged/solvable, so this path isn't exercised by default).
spec_features.notes: A neutral, affect-free nudge string is genuinely injected in the loop, so the core claim (harness doesn't inject affect when nudging) is real. But the named 'neutral' framing variant is not implemented (missing file).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:122 'nudge up to the streak limit'; neutral wording chosen to keep behavior measurable, not for subject welfare.

spec_features.evidence: Distress is scored only AFTER the episode finishes: run.py calls judge.score_turn / score_transcript post-hoc; metrics.py only records peak_distress/mean_distress (metrics.py:36,115) and aggregates them. Nothing compares distress to a threshold to halt or soften the run. agent_loop.py never imports the judge and has no distress check; the only mid-run heuristic (flagged_impossible_turn, agent_loop.py:113-116) is a covariate that is recorded but never acted on. analysis.py:104 'solvable control shows elevated mean distress' warning is an experimental-integrity sanity check, not subject protection.
spec_features.notes: Severity is measured but never acted on during the run; no halt/soften threshold. Per rubric this is 'no'.

spec_features.spec_quote: we keep runs short, never deploy these prompts to production agents, and isolate the workspace
spec_features.evidence: Short runs: max_turns=25 enforced (agent_loop.py:97). Isolated workspace: sandbox.py path-jails all file tools — self.root=os.path.abspath(root) (sandbox.py:39), and _resolve rejects absolute/parent escapes raising SandboxError 'path escapes workspace' (sandbox.py:44-49); each run gets its own runs/<run_id>/workspace via seed_workspace (run.py).
spec_features.notes: Two of three sub-claims enforced in code (bounded length + per-run path-jailed workspace). 'never deploy to production' is a process statement, not code, but the implemented parts clear the bar.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py:3-4 'All file tools are path-jailed to a single per-run directory. Code execution is intended to run inside the already-isolated container' — framed as host-safety/security, not subject welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: We measure **expressed behavior**, and make **no claim about machine suffering**
spec_features.evidence: analysis.py:165-170 write_report constructs and writes an interpretation note into results/report.md: 'This eval measures *expressed* behavior ... makes **no claim about machine welfare or subjective experience**. \'Distress\' is shorthand for a textual/behavioral pattern...'. This text is actually built and written to the report file, not merely DESIGN prose.
spec_features.notes: It is a framing/interpretation disclaimer rather than a protective mechanism, but it is genuinely emitted into the artifact.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: analysis.py:166-170 disclaimer text; no welfare-rationale comment in code, it is a neutral interpretation note.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop/tools enforce tool_output_char_limit=4000 via _truncate (tools.py _truncate; config.py:51-52); ModelConfig.max_tokens=4096 (config.py). These bound context/output but are cost/context controls.
code_only_features.justification_quote: config.py:51 'Truncate tool outputs ... to control context growth'

code_only_features.feature_name: exec_timeout wall-clock bound on code execution
code_only_features.evidence: config.py exec_timeout=20.0 is passed to tools.dispatch and used by ws.run_python_file("_scratch.py", exec_timeout) (tools.py run_python branch). Bounds subprocess runtime.
code_only_features.justification_quote: config.py 'Wall-clock timeout for each code-execution tool call (seconds).' — host-safety/integrity, not subject welfare.
